approach: Build the drain fix-request work (it is not in this base) and answer the six findings. (1) pin.rs: the checker's own problems become `SourceReport.findings: Vec<SourceFinding>` (study, file, kind, statement, evidence, anchor). The anchor is computed from data the code already holds, the `StudyText`: the statement is matched, after whitespace and case normalisation, against the string fields of the JSON entries in that file, and the innermost entry with an `id` or `term` names the anchor. Only when nothing matches does the anchor fall back to an FNV-1a hash of the normalised statement. Evidence is not in the key. Process failures ('did not report reading this file', 'could not be checked') are not findings and queue nothing. (2) steward.rs: `finding_marker` builds `Source fix: studies/<study>/<file> <kind> <anchor>` once and runs it through `plain_boundary_text`; that same string is the request title and the lookup key, and the anchor holds only [A-Za-z0-9._+-] or `h`+hex. `source_fix_request` builds the text only through `StewardRequest::new`, with path-like words in the statement and evidence defanged so `request_text_touches` returns only the study file. `citing_request` finds a non-closed job whose first line equals the marker. (3) drain.rs `RealSteps::check_page`: after the source check, queue one request per finding that has no open request (checked against records at head and against markers already queued in this call). Pass/fail and `Check::detail` do not change. A request queued here is on channel cli, so the run's next `steps.queue()` (drain.rs:3084) lists it and the same run plans and works it if the budget fits. That is the chosen behavior: a held-back page is fixed by the run that found the problem. A drain-level test shows it with the production `RealSteps::queue`. (4) claims.json c45: the pinned source is not in this copy (Glob finds no fm-teardown.sh, no pinned-source/), so the Queued line cannot be read. Unless the producer finds it, c45 is re-cited at the two already-validated reopen quotes (fm-teardown.sh line 30, fm-backlog-transition-lib.sh line 54). The CHANGELOG says plainly that those lines do not say Queued and that the Queued return was not checked against the pinned source. (5) model.json and intro.json are verified by Grep: Grep finds 'final state' only in the `done` glossary entry (intro.json:83) and 'terminal' only as the `done` kind (model.json:9); reopened is `waiting` and t12 goes reopened to queued. They are edited only if a leftover turns up. (6) Tests and CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Anchor the dedup key on the study's own entries: normalise the reported statement and find the innermost JSON entry (with an `id` or `term`) in the reported file whose string field contains it, or is contained by it (shorter side at least 12 characters). That entry's id is the anchor; several matches give their sorted ids joined with '+', at most 3. Fall back to an FNV-1a hash of the normalised statement. Evidence is never in the key.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1. The checker quotes the statement (pin.rs:352-356), and for claims.json that quote is the claim's text, so the entry that holds it gives a stable id without the model naming one. The code already holds the StudyText, and the match does not depend on the model's evidence prose, which changes between runs. FNV-1a by hand is stable across builds, unlike DefaultHasher.

rejected.option: Claim id parsed from the statement, then cited path and lines parsed from evidence, then a hash
rejected.why: The statement rarely names an id, and evidence is free prose the model rewrites each run, so the same contradiction would be queued again.

rejected.option: Key on file and kind only
rejected.why: A new contradiction in the same file would never be queued.

rejected.option: Key on the full statement text
rejected.why: A reworded statement that matches no entry still gets a new key; matching to an entry is more stable, and the hash is only the last resort.

decisions.choice: Build the marker once with `finding_marker` (through `plain_boundary_text`) and use that single string both as the request title and as the lookup key in `citing_request`. The anchor is restricted to [A-Za-z0-9._+-] (else the hash form), so it holds no words.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. `StewardRequest::new` rewords the title (steward.rs:544), so a raw marker could differ from the stored first line and be queued on every run. A unit test checks that `render()` of a request starts with exactly the marker, and that `citing_request` finds a job queued from it.

rejected.why: It would miss a reworded stored title and queue a duplicate on every run.

rejected.option: Refuse a finding whose marker needs rewording
rejected.why: Study and file names with a boundary word are already refused as a path by `StewardRequest::new`; a second refusal rule adds nothing.

decisions.choice: A fix request queued by check_page is worked in the same run that queued it. The plan, a test and the CHANGELOG say so.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. The run loop calls `steps.queue()` after each wave (drain.rs:3084) and `RealSteps::queue` lists channel-cli requests through `steward::queued_work` (drain.rs:4363). Filtering the request out would leave a held-back page unfixed until a later run, and the drain exists to get the page right. The budget guards in `batches_for` and `prepare` still bound the spend. The new test calls the production `RealSteps::queue` after `check_page` and sees the job in the QueueView items and the plan, with no open question (the touched file exists at base).

rejected.option: Defer or filter Source fix requests out of the same run

risks.risk: The model paraphrases a statement so that it matches no entry in the file. The anchor then falls back to the hash, and the same contradiction can be queued again.
risks.mitigation: Matching tolerates case, spacing and containment in either direction, and the evidence is not in the key. A miss costs one extra open request, never a wrong pass or fail. The CHANGELOG states the limit.

risks.risk: A statement that quotes two entries (kind behavior) gets a joined id such as 't9+t12'. If the model quotes only one of them next run, the key changes.
risks.mitigation: Only matched ids are used and they are sorted. The risk is named in the CHANGELOG; the effect is one extra request.

risks.risk: Existing drain tests that run the real check with a failing fake checker now commit request records, which could change commit counts or `Records` assertions in tests/drain.rs.
risks.mitigation: The commit happens only when the fake reports a problem, and only inside `RealSteps::check_page`. `cargo test -p athena-cli` and `cargo test` (criteria 4 and 6) are the check; tests/drain.rs is a deliverable and any assertion the new commit breaks is updated there.

risks.risk: The same-run pickup spends budget on the fix job after a held-back check, and a fix that fails is re-queued by a later check.
risks.mitigation: `batches_for` and `prepare` apply the run's budget guards to the new job like any other. A re-queue happens only after another landing and a rating at the target, because that is when check_page runs. The CHANGELOG states both.

risks.risk: c45 cannot be matched to a line that says Queued in this environment, so the real source check may flag c45 and queue one fix request on the next drain.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG says plainly that the cited lines do not say Queued and that the pinned source was not read. The Host question asks for the mount. The queued finding would be skipped on every later run while open.

risks.risk: Queueing fails (a boundary word in a study or file name, a redaction change, a records commit error) and would abort the check.
risks.mitigation: The marker is word-free by construction. A build or queue error is appended to the check detail and never changes pass or fail.

risks.risk: The model-backed check against the real pin cannot run here, so 'the drain source check passes on the corrected study' is not shown.
risks.mitigation: Criterion 3's demonstration records the route the conventions test prints and does not claim the source check ran. The CHANGELOG states which part was not run.

demonstrations.method: New drain test `source_fix_queues_one_request_per_contradiction_and_none_while_open` in tests/drain.rs. It uses `Fixture::new()`, `commit_study` with the demo study (claims.json is `[{id: c1, text: ...}]`), and `RealSteps { athena, ui: &Quiet, page: &StubPage, lander }`. The fake `SourceJudge` closure counts its calls with an AtomicUsize and returns files_checked plus: call 1 one `contradicted` problem whose statement is a fragment of c1's text with NO claim id in it, evidence 'pinned-source/bin/x.sh lines 30-33'; call 2 the same fragment with different case and spacing and different evidence ('line 31, see also pinned-source/bin/y.sh'); call 3 that problem plus a second one quoting a different claim c2 in the same file. The test calls the production `check_page()` three times and loads `Records::load` at head after each. It checks: after run 1 exactly one request job whose first line is `Source fix: studies/demo/claims.json contradicted c1`; after run 2 still one; after run 3 two, the second ending ` c2`. Run 1's request text holds the statement and the defanged evidence, an `Acceptance:` section and `Files: studies/demo/claims.json`, and `request_text_touches` of it is only that file. `athena_core::steward::citing_request` returns the job. The Check is still failed with `demo/claims.json` and the statement in its detail. After run 1, the production `steps.queue()` (RealSteps::queue, drain.rs:4339) lists the job in `items` and `plan`, with no open question: this is the same-run pickup of finding 2. A second test checks that a 'did not report reading' problem queues nothing, and that a closed request (landed or abandoned) is queued again. Core unit tests: steward.rs `source_fix_*` (marker equality across reworded statements, difference across entries and kinds, marker equals the first line of the built request, request text, open versus closed with the `Records::default()` pattern near steward.rs:2320) and pin.rs `source_finding_*` (anchor from a claims.json entry, from an intro.json glossary term, from a model.json transition, hash fallback, non-JSON file). The refusal corpus is not involved: this is not a reading refusal or matching rule, and `StewardRequest::new`'s checks are unchanged.
